sections.title: Employment Contract
sections.text:
Pedro. A name so common it is always overlooked.

He strives to understand those who walk toward death, yet has never expected anyone to understand him.

sections.title: Token
sections.text: A communicator of seemingly basic design, which he has tuned and modified for interference resistance. Carry it, and perhaps you'll never have to worry about losing track of him — or forgetting him.

sections.title: Profile
sections.text: Pedro, a Bolívarian. He was conscripted by several different True Bolívarian units, usually taking part in operations as a guerrilla or an intelligence officer. He left the True Bolívarian forces after the Great March in Bolívar, and now cooperates with Rhodes Island, assisting with certain intelligence work.

sections.title: Clinical Analysis
sections.text:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Pedro shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.08u/L
Operator Pedro rarely comes into contact with Originium.

I take issue with this part of the record. When he arrived, he was carrying a crossbow bolt of True Bolívarian make—if you ask me, that thing was nothing but an Oripathy dirty bomb. Merely storing and carrying it involved a degree of risk, and we only disposed of it during the hazardous materials registration check. What is more, he clearly knew that thing inside and out. How is this 'rarely comes into contact' in any way?
—A Logistics Department Operator questioning the recorded content

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
A considerable number of the warlords and guerrilla bands among the True Bolívarians have no qualms about raising or hiring child soldiers, and Pedro appears to have been one of those child soldiers. We have no standing to interfere unduly in this—all the more so when the True Bolívarians publicly maintain that every child soldier volunteered to resist foreign invaders and defend their own homeland.
According to Operator Pedro, he did indeed volunteer of his own accord, his reason being that he 'wanted even one more person to survive.' As for why he moved repeatedly between various warlords and organizations, it was because 'the comrades who died in battle said you could not see Bolívar's future here.'
We are troubled by the circumstances of these child soldiers. We also note with regret that, before they were swept onto the battlefield by slogans and mobilization orders, they clearly had no chance to receive an education sufficient to let them fully consider and understand their own lives and this land.
更令人痛心的，则是我们并没有立场仅去谴责那些军阀对待自己的同胞的方式。这些少年兵中有许多人都曾在内外敌对势力的侵略中失去亲人与家园，最后变得走投无路而看不到任何得救的希望，参军几乎是他们唯一活下去的方法。训练他们的军人也生于同样的战乱中，若这些少年能熬过饥荒、疾病与战火并长大成人，恐怕他们自己也会成为训练下一批少年兵的人……愿为私利而反复上演的侵略终会止息，而我们也将始终致力于保卫每个人生命的尊严。

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
In point of fact, a few curious little episodes occurred over the course of Operator Pedro's combat testing.
尽管他表现出来的能力几乎与其他接受过标准战斗训练的武装部队人员无异，我是说，虽然这件事对一名少年兵来说或许也不容易，但还不是那么离奇。离奇的地方在于那些难以仅用参数涵盖的部分——除了最尖端的那些，他能够熟练地使用各种制式武器，并且在弩箭等多种手持远程打击武器的使用上，准头好得惊人，甚至能在转移过程中精准地命中移动标靶的靶心。此外，所有关于潜入行动的处理也非常干净利落，不留破绽。虽然这种事情上或许的确有天才，但他的情况比起天才应该更像是熟练度极高的样子……真不敢相信，这些少年兵过的到底是什么样的生活？

Addendum: Do not let me catch any of you giggling your way over to an Operator of his age with an apple on your head after learning the results of these tests. Suction-cup arrows are not acceptable either. Kroos, at least, would never pick her targets for pranks as thoughtlessly as you lot do.

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
We had always assumed that Operator Pedro would have had little opportunity for a decent general education before coming to Rhodes Island, yet judging by his performance in these classes, that does not seem to be the case. We deliberately prepared test material that went beyond the syllabus, and he answered a portion of those questions correctly as well. He also learns unfamiliar material remarkably quickly. He is lacking only in imagination, and struggles with things he has never actually seen and with certain abstract concepts. On the whole, however, he remains a boy in whom his teachers take great comfort and fondness.
Only on questions concerning certain parts of the modern history of Bolívar, Iberia, and Columbia does Operator Pedro frequently fail to answer correctly. We are not certain whether this stems from the influence of ideas instilled in him by the True Bolívarians, or whether traumatic experiences leave him unable to accept what the textbooks teach. At this stage, however, we believe he should not be forced to accept the history in the books; giving him an open space instead may be more conducive to his growth.
We have also noticed that Operator Pedro seems quite poor at discovering on his own what he wants to do, yet the moment he is given a task and told the reason it needs doing, he shows no shortage of initiative whatsoever. This does not seem reducible to simple numbness of spirit, and we do not truly understand how such a disposition came about. Even so, we cannot help hoping that a boy would have some things he wants to do of his own accord—even if it is only to play to his heart's content.

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
There is something not quite normal about Operator Pedro. I must make clear that I mean to express no prejudice whatsoever, but when I tried, exactly as I always do when compiling any other Operator's file, to observe and record his life and relationships at Rhodes Island, I truly found myself at a loss. It is as though he does not exist here at all—though I suspect that phrasing is not accurate either. It would be better to say that, were it not for the nature of my work, I would never have thought of him at all, and I am afraid the same holds true for the other Operators.
I have heard tales and anecdotes of legendary intelligence officers—that they can keep people from accurately identifying or recalling their faces. But Operator Pedro is something else again. Every Operator who has had contact with him remembers his features clearly, and there is nothing antisocial about his conduct; Operator Pedro will even accommodate every reasonable request made of him as far as he possibly can. And yet the Operators all voiced a certain bewilderment—they seem entirely unable to sense Operator Pedro's likes and dislikes while spending time with him, and some even have the illusion that at some point they and Operator Pedro politely distanced themselves from one another. As for the Operators who worked with him in combat exercises, they report that although they completed every objective together flawlessly, they cannot recall in the slightest when or how they came to coordinate with him.
After reviewing some activity footage and combat footage, I am quite certain that Operator Pedro is not being isolated by the other Operators, nor is he deliberately keeping his distance from us. But when I suddenly realized today that I had very nearly omitted the relationship observation report on Operator Pedro altogether, I could not help finding the matter strange.
I record all this not to promote some notion of collectivism—I quite agree that demanding an introverted person come to love group activities 'from the heart' is, in substance, a form of bullying. Even so, Operator Pedro's situation leaves me with a measure of concern, and if at all possible, I would like to obtain more professional opinions and support.

sections.title: Promotion Record
sections.text:
Death has no value, and no meaning. Not even the most magnificent death. Not the death of a brave man, nor the death of a coward; not the death of a good man, nor the death of a sinner.
Is an old man's death less to be mourned than a child's? Is an Infected's death less to be mourned than a non-Infected's?
No death can bring anything at all. An upright courtier sacrificing himself to kill a tyrant does not amount to justice; a brave soldier sacrificing himself to kill a general does not amount to peace.
People commemorate for ages the sacrifices made for an ideal. I watched those sacrifices with my own eyes.
But did they truly not want to live? Did they not want to go on practicing their ideals, and on the day those ideals came true, embrace every one of their comrades? Were they really willing to fall before the dawn arrived, to receive their comrades' offerings, and to become the one among them whose name most deserved to be remembered?
I have heard that answer from their own mouths, but no one wants to know it. A person who lives on and succeeds usually ends up either criticized for frittering away the rest of his life, or slandered by people who blow his flaws out of proportion. The dead never are.
But if that is how it goes, how is it any different from praising death, from glorifying death? If that is how it goes, then where is the value of life?
If accepting death as a price and a bargaining chip is what maturity means, then I would rather be a little immature.
